table.one_line_across_the_table: Five routes tested, five kills (four clean, one in substance). No seat leaves the 'one quarter, two' body; no seat gains a target; every gain in one measure was paid for one-for-one in another, as the batch-7 lemma says (old distances grow only where links between old sites are cut).

state_of_the_geometry_keystone: THE GEOMETRY KEYSTONE AFTER BATCH 18 (seven seats, each checked once by a distinct same-family checker whose verdict governs; ONE MODEL FAMILY; nothing turns green). (1) IS THERE ANY GROWN BODY NEAR 3 ON BOTH RULERS, OR ON THE SLICE UNDER PD-20? NO. In no run of any seat and none of the checkers' fresh-seed runs. The walk ruler stays about 2 (1.3-2.5); readings near or past 3 occur only as climbs in over-joined bodies, the random-network signature. The label is met only in passing or beside a walk of about 2. On the slice, the PD-20 target fails on every grown body tested, the principal's own reading (two carriers, any unfired site, with and without a mark-reading preference) included: slices by age fall apart into dust. The only bodies near 3 on both rulers are supplied (the diamond start, runs frozen at the written start, a slab of a toy history): inputs that earn nothing. (2) DEAD AS TESTED (checked once): (a) a single Birth preferring cuts between still pieces, reading lasting marks 0-2 steps away - +0.0125 against the 0.05 needed, and at a flat seam no tight Birth can thin it at all (exact); (b) the seal under the principal's carrier rule - no carrier speed gives separate still pieces in stretching space, and using carriers up seals the network (exact count); (c) seams that gain links through Births, on the designed body - walk and stretch trade at the seams, and random Births do as well as targeted ones; (d) the slice re-reading as a rescue for the bodies on file; (e) rings as native still pieces - they live a quarter of a doubling. Both routes batch 11 left open are therefore closed in the forms its chair specified. (3) WHAT THE FIVE KILLS HAVE IN COMMON (chair synthesis, labelled, no credit): every route changed WHICH links a Birth cuts or WHERE Births happen; none changed what a Birth builds. Three exact facts now bracket the problem. First, the twin always joins all four of its owner's neighbours whatever their age, so the body is a reworked present (long-link share about one half) and no cut choice can make it a history. Second, tight Births at a seam can only re-route or thicken it, never thin it, and they feed on their own newborns. Third, the one native move that adds links without adding sites - the undo's swap - adds them to every link alike and, unstopped, scrambles any geometry within a fraction of a swap per site. So the body sits between two failures: Births alone give 'one quarter, two'; the swap alone gives the random tangle; 3 on the walk ruler is crossed between them and never held. (4) WHAT IS LEFT (named by seats and checkers; all untested on grown material): the undo live at growing tips together with what closes it - a link flip, a write, or burial under children (PD-24, PD-32); a mark handed down from the site that gave birth, read over the Birth's own eight sites; Births acting together across a gap; growth placed in the seams rather than cuts chosen there; a growth front whose whole neighbourhood is young (the only way to a true history, and PD-30 points the other way); a ring census to decide whether the body is a crumpled sheet. (5) A TENSION TO DECIDE, NOT A RESULT: the coordinator's target (about 3 on a slice, about 4 on the whole history) assumes grown bodies are histories; the checked evidence says they are presents, and the hydrogen idea seat adds (checked once, on toys) that an atom's 1/n^2 ladder needs the links that still flip to read 3 - on a live four-reading history there is no bound level at all at placeholder values. Both lines point to reading the shifting network as present space. That choice changes what the card must show, so it is put as question 1.

ready_seat_specs.title: THE UNDO AT GROWING TIPS AND WHAT CLOSES IT
ready_seat_specs.card_or_keystone: three dimensions; keystones 'A built-in reworking move that needs a stop', 'The geometry the records grow into'
ready_seat_specs.source_ideas: IGS-01, IGS-02, IGS-03; the IGS checker's first choice; PD-24, PD-32
ready_seat_specs.why: Every growth run on file leaves the undo out, yet it is in the rules and, unstopped, erases a diamond's label within a quarter of a swap per site. It is also the only native move that adds links without adding sites. Whether grown material is frozen or liquid is unknown.
ready_seat_specs.compute: The common growth protocol with rights only at growth points (PD-06, PD-30), the tip undo with its swap under children-first, and three scanned rates per Birth attempt on a registered grid: undo (0, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9), write (1, 0.1, 0.01), flip lock on a newborn link (0, 0.1, 1, 10). To 64x, two seeds. Report both rulers, old-pair stretch and evenness, links across marked seams, the share of Births still undoable, and the shape of the frozen set.
ready_seat_specs.what_kills_it: Both rulers within 0.25 and the stretch within 0.03 of the undo-off body at every grid point (the undo changes nothing), or every grid point that differs only climbs toward the random-network control with old distances shrinking.
